question.problem: Calculate the flux of the vector field $F(x,y)=xi+\frac{1}{4}\,j$ across the closed curve $C$ given by $r(t)=4\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+8\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j$ for $t\in [0,2\pi ).$
question.worked_solution:
If $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ is a vector field and $C$ is a piecewise-smooth, simple, closed curve, then the flux of $F$ across $C$ is given by

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s={∮}_{C}P\,\text{d}y-Q\,\text{d}x,
$$

where $n$ denotes the outward-pointing unit normal vector to $C.$ 

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=4\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y=8\operatorname{sin}⁡t.
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(x,y) & =x=4\operatorname{cos}⁡t, \\ Q(x,y) & =\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the derivatives of $x(t)$ and $y(t)$ along the curve, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4\operatorname{cos}⁡t)=-4\operatorname{sin}⁡t, \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(8\operatorname{sin}⁡t)=8\operatorname{cos}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral using the double-angle formula for cosine, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s & ={∮}_{C}P\,\text{d}y-Q\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }(P\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}-Q\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }(4\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\cdot (8\operatorname{cos}⁡t)-(\frac{1}{4})\cdot (-4\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }32{cos}^{2}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }32(\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+1}{2})+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & =(8\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)+16t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t){|}_{0}^{2\pi } \\  & =(0+32\pi -1)-(0-1) \\  & =32\pi \end{aligned}
$$
